prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1365; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed initial report for left-turn collision at intersection. Insured states they turned left on a green arrow and the other vehicle entered from the opposing direction. Claimant reported back strain at scene and was transported by EMS. Photos requested from both drivers. Liability not yet determined.

Entry 2: Spoke with insured's recorded statement. Insured confirms signal phase and says oncoming vehicle was not visible until the last moment due to a parked truck blocking sight lines. Requested scene diagram from the responding officer. Will cross-check against traffic camera availability.

Entry 3: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Received letter of representation and a request for the claimant's policy limits and medical authorization. Forwarded the request to the supervisor for handling under bodily injury protocol.

Entry 4: Obtained the responding officer's report. It cites the other driver for failure to yield on a left turn. Insured's version is consistent with the officer's account on signal phase. Preliminary liability assessment leans toward the other party at roughly 70 percent, pending review of the scene diagram and witness contact.

Entry 5: Received treatment records from the claimant's attorney covering urgent care and a follow-up with a physical therapist. Diagnosis listed as lumbar strain with no fracture noted on imaging. Records reviewed and placed in the injury file. Next step is to schedule an independent medical review and confirm whether the claimant has returned to work.
